beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Consider a consultant asking a Research Robot to compare supplier proposals.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The assistant returns a clear table and a confident recommendation.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: At first glance, the assignment appears finished.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: But one price is monthly, another annual, and a contract condition is missing.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A polished answer can conceal the very uncertainty the consultant needs to see.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book asks what makes this work inspectable before anyone acts on it.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: That question turns a familiar AI example into a design problem.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: It also shows why the book spends time on evidence, versions, and human judgment.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: An especially useful distinction separates a proposed result from an accepted one.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The latest file may still contain claims nobody has checked.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Accepting the supplier comparison approves a particular version of that report.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: It does not automatically authorize a purchase.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: This small distinction changes what another worker may safely assume.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book follows these relationships through documents, source material, and derived results.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: You learn to ask what was reviewed, by whom, and for which purpose.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: That is a more precise question than whether the assistant sounded convincing.
